The second copy does nothing meaningful — they don't need a backup Grindstone when the first is still in play (it's legendary-irrelevant but redundant). More importantly, they should be deploying Goblin Welder or Goblin Engineer first, as these are the key combo pieces that enable the Painter's Servant/Grindstone interaction and artifact recursion. Playing the redundant Grindstone wastes mana and a card slot when they could be advancing their game plan with creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a second Grindstone from hand when one was already on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain for the land drop, then cast Goblin Welder (1 mana) and Goblin Engineer (2 mana) to establish the artifact recursion engine. The second Grindstone is redundant and wastes a turn's worth of development.

annotations.description: Discarded Mountain instead of the redundant Grindstone. They already have Grindstone on the battlefield, making the second copy low-value. The Mountain would provide a crucial third land drop, enabling them to cast Goblin Engineer while retaining mana for protection spells like Pyroblast, or deploying multiple cheap threats in the same turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mountain
annotations.betterLine: Discard the redundant Grindstone, keeping Mountain for the next land drop to enable better sequencing of Goblin Engineer + protection/follow-up plays.

annotations.description: With the opponent on only 2 lands (Great Furnace + Mountain), using Wasteland to destroy Great Furnace would cut them to 1 land, severely constraining their ability to deploy combo pieces or activate Grindstone (which costs 3 to activate). Coach already has 5 lands and doesn't need a 6th. Destroying Great Furnace also removes an artifact relevant for potential Goblin Welder/Engineer synergies.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Flooded Strand as a 6th land instead of using Wasteland.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Great Furnace to mana-screw the opponent and remove an artifact land, then play Flooded Strand from hand as the land drop.

annotations.description: Failing to use Wasteland to destroy Great Furnace would leave the opponent with 2 mana sources and an artifact land that synergizes with Goblin Welder/Engineer. Cutting the opponent to just 1 Mountain severely hampers their ability to activate Grindstone (costs 3) or deploy combo pieces.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Flooded Strand to fetch a land instead of using Wasteland to destroy Great Furnace
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Great Furnace to cut opponent to 1 mana source and remove an artifact, then crack Flooded Strand if needed later

annotations.description: With 2 Tundras already in play plus Meticulous Archive and Island providing ample color coverage, fetching a basic Plains would be superior to a third Tundra. Basic Plains is immune to Wasteland while still casting the three Swords to Plowshares in hand. In Legacy, protecting against Wasteland by fetching basics when color requirements are already met is fundamental.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Tundra (a third copy) instead of basic Plains
annotations.betterLine: Fetch basic Plains to have Wasteland-proof white mana source, since blue mana is already well-covered by existing lands

annotations.description: Fetched Tundra instead of basic Plains when already having 4 blue sources (2 Tundra, Meticulous Archive, Island). With 3 Swords to Plowshares in hand as the primary need, a basic Plains provides the same white mana while being immune to Wasteland, which is common in Legacy.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Tundra from library
annotations.betterLine: Fetch basic Plains to protect against Wasteland while still having ample blue mana from existing lands

annotations.description: Goblin Engineer is one of the key combo pieces that enables the Painter's Servant/Grindstone combo by tutoring artifacts into the graveyard and reanimating them. Discarding it significantly reduces the ability to assemble the combo. Meanwhile, the second copy of Grindstone is redundant since one is already on the battlefield, and Great Furnace is a land that could be played but is less critical than a combo enabler.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Goblin Engineer to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard the second Grindstone (already have one on the battlefield) or Great Furnace. Goblin Engineer is essential for the combo plan as it can tutor Painter's Servant and swap artifacts from the graveyard.

annotations.description: GPT5m Villain has 3 Lightning Bolts in hand and the opponent is at 16 life. With 2 Mountains and 2 Great Furnaces (after playing this one), they have access to 4 red mana. They could cast 2 Lightning Bolts this turn for 6 damage (opponent to 10), saving the third for next turn. However, the opponent has 7 lands untapped including multiple blue sources, meaning Daze and Force of Will are live. Playing Great Furnace first to have more mana available is reasonable sequencing. The real question is whether Goblin Welder should be prioritized here - Welder enables the combo with Grindstone (by welding artifacts) and there's a Goblin Engineer in the graveyard. But Welder itself doesn't immediately combo without Painter's Servant or similar. Playing the land is fine, but casting Goblin Welder this turn could be important to start pressuring the combo angle, especially since the opponent could Wasteland a land next turn. The play of Great Furnace is reasonable as it enables more options next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Great Furnace as land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Playing Great Furnace is fine as a land drop, but should strongly consider casting Goblin Welder with the available red mana this turn to establish a board presence and potential combo threat, or fire off Lightning Bolts at end of opponent's turn to apply pressure while they might tap out.

annotations.description: Casting a redundant second Grindstone (without Painter's Servant to combo with) instead of using available mana to advance the game plan. With 3 Lightning Bolts in hand and the opponent at 16 life, burn should be the priority. A second Grindstone on the battlefield provides minimal value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Grindstone (second copy) during combat, deploying a redundant combo piece with no combo enabler available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Bolt targeting the opponent (16 -> 13 life), progressing the burn plan. With 3 Bolts in hand representing 9 damage, every point matters. Goblin Welder could also be deployed to set up artifact recursion.

annotations.description: Stoneforge Mystic has an activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}) that can put an Equipment card from hand onto the battlefield, which would cost only 2 mana instead of 5. By hardcasting Batterskull for 5 mana, Gem3F Coach wastes 3 extra mana and doesn't use the key advantage of having Stoneforge Mystic in play. Additionally, hardcasting Batterskull is more vulnerable to countermagic, whereas Stoneforge's ability puts it directly onto the battlefield. Using Stoneforge's ability would also leave mana open for Daze, Force of Will, or Swords to Plowshares.
annotations.actionTaken: Hardcast Batterskull for 5 mana
annotations.betterLine: Use Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}) to put Batterskull onto the battlefield for only 2 mana, leaving up 3+ mana for interaction (Swords to Plowshares, Daze, etc.)

annotations.description: Discarded Pithing Needle, which could name Stoneforge Mystic to prevent it from cheating Batterskull into play - a critical upcoming threat. The duplicate Grindstone is largely redundant since one is already on the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Pithing Needle
annotations.betterLine: Discard the second Grindstone, as one is already on the battlefield. Keep Pithing Needle to name Stoneforge Mystic next turn for just 1 mana, preventing the Batterskull activation.

annotations.description: Coach passed without activating Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Great Furnaces. The opponent only has 3 lands (2 Great Furnace + 1 Mountain), and destroying a Great Furnace would both cut their mana to 2 sources and remove an artifact that could be used in Welder/Engineer sacrifice chains. Coach has 7 lands and can easily afford to sacrifice Wasteland.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without taking any action in postcombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting a Great Furnace to cut the opponent's mana and remove an artifact from the battlefield, limiting their ability to execute artifact synergies.

annotations.description: Failed to use Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Great Furnaces when the opponent only has 3 lands. Destroying a Great Furnace would mana-screw the opponent (leaving them with just 2 lands), remove an artifact that could be relevant for Welder/Engineer interactions, and the Coach has plenty of mana (7 lands) to afford sacrificing Wasteland.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without taking any action in precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting one of the opponent's Great Furnaces to cut them off mana and reduce artifact count, while still having 6 lands which is more than enough to operate.

annotations.description: GPT5m Villain has Grindstone on the battlefield and a second Grindstone in hand, plus Goblin Welder in hand. Goblin Welder is a key combo piece that can recur artifacts from the graveyard (like Painter's Servant if they find one, or reuse Grindstone). It's also a creature that enables the Welder's activated ability to swap artifacts between battlefield and graveyard. Discarding Goblin Welder removes a critical engine piece. Meanwhile, the opponent has Pithing Needle in the Villain's graveyard (which was likely naming something important), and Goblin Engineer is also in the graveyard. Goblin Welder could potentially recur Goblin Engineer or other artifacts. A Mountain is a much safer discard since the Villain already has 4 lands on the battlefield (2 Great Furnaces + 2 Mountains) and 2 more Mountains in hand - they have plenty of mana sources.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Goblin Welder
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Mountain instead, keeping Goblin Welder as a combo/utility piece that can swap artifacts between battlefield and graveyard, enabling recursion of key pieces like Goblin Engineer or Pithing Needle.

annotations.description: Declined to put Batterskull onto the battlefield via Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability. This is the primary purpose of playing Stoneforge Mystic - cheating a 5-mana equipment into play for 2 mana. Batterskull would create a 4/4 vigilance lifelink Germ token, presenting a fast clock against an opponent at 10 life with no creatures and no way to interact with it.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined Stoneforge Mystic's ability, keeping Batterskull stranded in hand where it costs 5 mana to cast normally.
annotations.betterLine: Put Batterskull onto the battlefield via Stoneforge Mystic's ability, creating a 4/4 vigilance lifelink creature that would close the game in 2-3 attacks.

annotations.description: Gem3F Coach has Flooded Strand available to play as a land drop but chose to pass without playing it. Missing a land drop is leaving free resources on the table, especially with a fetchland that provides deck thinning and color fixing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing Flooded Strand or taking any action.
annotations.betterLine: Play Flooded Strand as land for turn. Even if not immediately needed, having an extra fetchland available provides flexibility and can be cracked at instant speed later for deck thinning or to fix mana.

annotations.description: GPT5m Villain is at 10 life facing an opponent at 24 life with Stoneforge Mystic on board (likely fetching/putting Batterskull into play). The villain has 3 Lightning Bolts in hand (9 damage total) which represents a realistic burn kill plan. Urza's Saga is one of the most powerful cards in the deck - it creates Construct tokens that grow with artifacts (already has 2 Great Furnaces + Grindstone = 3 artifacts), and its chapter III can tutor for a 0-1 cost artifact. Meanwhile, a Mountain is a basic land that provides the same red mana but without any of Urza's Saga's powerful abilities. The villain should be discarding a Mountain instead, preserving Urza's Saga as a way to create board presence and potentially tutor for useful artifacts.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Urza's Saga
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Mountain instead, keeping Urza's Saga which creates growing Construct tokens (with 3+ artifacts already in play) and tutors for artifacts on chapter III, providing a much stronger path to victory alongside the burn plan.

annotations.description: Gem3F Coach passed their precombat main phase without activating Stoneforge Mystic to put Batterskull (or Cryptic Coat) onto the battlefield. The opponent is at 10 life with no creatures, and deploying a 4/4 vigilance lifelink Germ token would create a fast clock while gaining life. There's no strategic reason to hold back the equipment when the opponent has minimal board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the precombat main phase without taking any action.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Stoneforge Mystic to put Batterskull onto the battlefield, creating a 4/4 vigilance lifelink token. This applies immediate pressure against the opponent at 10 life while the hand has Force of Will and Daze to protect against any response. Could also consider using Wasteland on a Great Furnace to constrain opponent's mana.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 1 life with exactly 3 mana sources (Mountain + 2 Great Furnace) to activate Grindstone ({3}, {T}). Wasteland could destroy a Great Furnace to cut them off Grindstone activation mana, removing their primary win condition for essentially free.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using Wasteland, leaving opponent with exactly enough mana to activate Grindstone.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting a Great Furnace to cut opponent to 2 mana, preventing Grindstone activation and eliminating their combo win condition.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 1 life with exactly 3 mana sources (2 Great Furnace + Mountain), which is exactly enough to activate Grindstone (costs {3}, {T}). Using Wasteland to destroy a land would cut them to 2 mana, preventing Grindstone activation even if they find Painter's Servant to combo. With the opponent's only win condition being the Grindstone combo, this is a meaningful disruption opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without using Wasteland or casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's lands (preferably Great Furnace to also reduce artifact count), cutting them off from activating Grindstone and making it nearly impossible for them to combo before dying to Stoneforge Mystic attacks.
